2608.30935.title: LightNav-0: Eliciting VLM Spatial Intelligence for Generalist Embodied Navigation
2608.30935.paper_summary: Embodied navigation requires agents to translate heterogeneous goals and visual observations into actions across tasks, environments, and robot embodiments. Modern vision-language models (VLMs) already encode spatial priors for visual grounding, spatial reasoning, and pointing, but these capabilities are rarely elicited directly for robot control. Existing navigation systems instead rely on task- or embodiment-specific components, fragmenting perception, reasoning, and action while offering limited generalization. Here we present LightNav-0, a compact generalist embodied navigation model that elicits the spatial intelligence of a pretrained VLM and aligns it with navigation, without task-specific prediction heads. LightNav-0 represents diverse navigation tasks through a unified token interface: dual-channel pointing expresses task-, scene-, and embodiment-agnostic spatial intent, while a residual vector-quantized action tokenizer maps this intent to precise, embodiment-specific trajectories. Together with temporally aware visual history compression, ER mid-training, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning, this formulation supports instruction following, open-vocabulary object navigation, and visual tracking within a single model. The navigation training corpus spans 2K+ scenes and 4K+ hours of embodied navigation data. LightNav-ER, the embodied-reasoning checkpoint used to initialize LightNav-0, attains the highest complete-set average across 8 embodied-reasoning benchmarks, while LightNav-0 achieves state-of-the-art monocular success rates across all 10 public navigation simulation settings. Real-world evaluations further demonstrate zero-shot generalization across robot embodiments, diverse scenes, and static and dynamic targets. These results establish compact VLMs as a unified and transferable backbone for generalist embodied navigation.
2608.30935.paper_summary_zh: 具身導航要求代理將異質目標和視覺觀察轉化為在任務、環境和機器人具身體中的行動。現代視覺-語言模型（VLMs）已經編碼了用於視覺基礎、空間推理和指向的空間先驗，但這些能力很少被直接用於機器人控制。現有的導航系統則依賴於特定任務或具身體的組件，分散了感知、推理和行動，同時提供有限的泛化能力。在此，我們介紹LightNav-0，一種緊湊的通用具身導航模型，它引發了預訓練VLM的空間智慧，並將其與導航對齊，而不使用特定任務的預測頭。LightNav-0通過統一的標記介面表示多樣的導航任務：雙通道指向表達任務、場景和具身體無關的空間意圖，而殘差向量量化行動標記器則將這一意圖映射到精確的具身體特定軌跡。結合時間感知的視覺歷史壓縮、ER中期訓練、監督微調和強化學習，這一公式支持指令跟隨、開放詞彙物體導航和視覺追蹤，均在單一模型中實現。導航訓練語料庫涵蓋2000多個場景和4000多小時的具身導航數據。LightNav-ER，作為初始化LightNav-0的具身推理檢查點，在8個具身推理基準中達到了最高的完整集平均值，而LightNav-0在所有10個公共導航模擬設置中實現了最先進的單眼成功率。現實世界的評估進一步證明了在機器人具身體、多樣場景以及靜態和動態目標之間的零樣本泛化。這些結果確立了緊湊的VLM作為通用具身導航的統一和可轉移的骨幹。
